model.name: DREAM S2 semantic news-cycle retention
model.lambda_interpretation: lambda = elapsed hours since semantic topic attention peak
model.abstraction_layer: Raw RSS articles are converted into stable semantic topic objects before S2 fitting.
model.semantic_layer: Sparse TF-IDF article vectors, entity sets, keyword distributions, semantic connected components, centroid inertia, and a persistent topic_memory.json file.
model.event_horizon_layer: H(t)=Deviation(t)*CrossScaleCoherence(t), with Deviation=observed/expected_S2 and CrossScaleCoherence from source-tier spread, source diversity, and semantic coherence. Pre-horizon alerts require high H and positive slope.
model.signal_preprocessing: Formal S2 fit uses circadian-corrected publish-time article counts: raw count divided by expected global publishing/activity factor.
model.observation_clock: article.published_at, not GitHub Action run time
model.history_role: data/history.json retains raw article records and first_seen/last_seen provenance; topic_memory.json retains semantic identity; cycles.json retains completed S2 cycle summaries.
model.comparison: Delta AIC = AIC(exponential beta=1) - AIC(stretched S2 beta free)
model.cycle_archive_role: data/cycles.json stores deduplicated completed formal cycle summaries so prior S2 learning remains visible when a new wave resets the current topic. Current waves are not archived until replaced by a new peak.

articles.title: This is how badly Trump’s Republican endorsements did in the midterms
articles.summary: The Guardian analyzed US Senate, House and governors’ races, showing Trump’s dwindling influence over the GOP Donald Trump often boasts about the power of his “Complete and Total Endorsement” of candidates, but in the 2026 midterms , his endorsements carried less weight than they did two years ago. Half of the Senate candidates Trump endorsed lost, and most of the governors the US president endorsed were defeated by Democratic candidates in this month’s blue wave midterm elections, according to an analysis by the Guardian. Continue reading...

articles.title: Race to lead Senate Democrats the latest battlefield in party’s tussle over Israel
articles.summary: Chris Van Hollen and Chuck Schumer represent conflicting visions on issue that has become ‘litmus test’ for Democratic voters The race to lead the Democratic Party’s incoming Senate majority has become the latest battlefield between two conflicting visions for how the US should relate to Israel – a once unquestioned ally whose collapsing standing among the US public has become a defining feature of American politics. Chuck Schumer, the veteran New York Senator and current Democratic minority leader, is one of Israel’s most reliable supporters in Congress. As he views it, according to an interview he gave last year, his “job” is to “keep the left pro-Israel”. Continue reading...
